findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A newcomer could repeat it after one read.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: This is the first section after the header, and it is an error message. The one place meant to show Athena's promised models, verdict and costs shows nothing, so the newcomer gets no evidence for the main claim and the page looks broken.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Athena's own site opens on a long study of a different project, firstmate. Almost all of the page (states, counters, twelve transition cards, a glossary of about 45 terms, 45 claims) is about firstmate's internals, which a newcomer to Athena did not come for.
findings.source: Page title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: What to do next is clear and concrete: the top of the page links to it, and the section lists prerequisites, the clone and install commands, and a first command to try. Supported operating systems are not stated.
findings.source: Header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link is shown to every visitor but only makes sense to the project owner. A newcomer may think they have to decide something.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The firstmate study is dense with terms like exit codes, places-held, captain call and transition ids. It is careful and well sourced, but a newcomer has to keep going back to the glossary just to see why the study is impressive.
findings.source: Transitions card t2: "Every worker place is held, so the spawn is deferred with exit 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: Several glossary entries (captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake) say the source does not define the term. That is honest, but it leaves the newcomer with undefined words.
findings.source: Glossary, entry for heartbeat: "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat."

findings.text: This section describes internal repository layout. It means nothing to a newcomer and does not say where studies/ lives.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
